description: A theory-inclined student with a strong interest in academic research who is transitioning from a Python-based introductory background to the rigors of C++ and formal algorithmic analysis.

nodes.title: Pointers and Memory Addresses
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student has no_prior_exposure to C++, this scaffolding node is essential for understanding the underlying memory model before building data structures.
nodes.description: Introduction to C++ pointer syntax and memory addresses, transitioning from high-level variable concepts to physical memory management.

nodes.title: C++ Dynamic Memory Lifecycle
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with no_prior_exposure to C++, mastering manual memory management is a prerequisite for the course's subsequent focus on custom-built structures.
nodes.description: Deep dive into the 'new' and 'delete' operators, manual memory allocation, and avoiding memory leaks in a C++ environment.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This scaffolding provides the necessary C++ syntactical context for a student with no_prior_exposure to the language's specific approach to object-oriented programming.
nodes.description: Translating general OOD principles into C++ specific syntax, including header (.h) vs implementation (.cpp) files and classes.
nodes.title: C++ Class Structure & Header Files

nodes.description: Advanced OOD in C++ focusing on inheritance hierarchies and the use of templates for generic programming.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Every student must master C++ templates and inheritance as they are fundamental to implementing generic data structures.
nodes.title: Templates and Inheritance
Linked List Implementation
nodes.description: Implementation and comparison of singly and doubly linked lists, focusing on node-based logic and iterator traversal.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Linked list implementation is a core competency required for all students in this cumulative curriculum.

nodes.description: First assessment checkpoint covering recursion principles and the fundamentals of Big-O asymptotic analysis.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This is a required assessment to ensure the student has mastered recursion and performance analysis before proceeding.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Big-O Analysis

nodes.description: Implementing stack and queue Abstract Data Types (ADTs) using both arrays and the C++ Standard Template Library.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mastery of stack and queue ADTs is fundamental to the course's sequence-based structure objectives.
nodes.title: Stack and Queue ADTs
Vectors and Iterators
nodes.description: Exploring the vector container, its dynamic resizing logic, and the standard iterator pattern for collection traversal.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required core content regarding the use of vectors and iterators as the primary means of navigating linear structures.

nodes.title: Sequence Sorting (Bubble Sort)
nodes.personalizationRationale: All students are examined on basic sorting performance as a precursor to more complex sorting algorithms later.
nodes.description: Introduction to sequence sorting through the bubble sort algorithm and its performance characteristics.
Comprehensive review of all material from Blocks 01 through 03 in preparation for the midterm examination.
nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory review checkpoint to ensure foundational material is solid before entering the theory-heavy trees blocks.
nodes.title: Midterm Exam Review (Blocks 1-3)

nodes.description: General tree structures and implementation of pre-order, post-order, and in-order traversal algorithms.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Tree traversal is a non-negotiable learning objective that every student must demonstrate.
nodes.title: Tree Traversals and Properties

nodes.description: Specialized properties of binary trees and their applications in representing hierarchical data.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Binary trees form the basis for search and balanced tree structures studied in later blocks.
nodes.title: Binary Tree Structures

nodes.personalizationRationale: Priority queues and heap-based implementations are a core requirement of the block 5 curriculum.
nodes.description: Implementation of heaps and their use in priority queue ADTs, including up-heap and down-heap operations.
nodes.title: Priority Queues and Heaps

nodes.personalizationRationale: Understanding hash tables is critical for achieving O(1) average-case lookups, a core course objective.
nodes.description: Design of hash functions, collision resolution strategies, and the skip list data structure.
nodes.title: Hash Tables and Skip Lists
Quiz 3: Maps and Dictionaries
nodes.description: Assessment of student understanding regarding maps, dictionaries, and hashing performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory assessment checkpoint for block 06 to verify dictionary-based knowledge.
Search tree mechanics are a core requirement of this proof-heavy block for all students.
nodes.description: Formal study of Binary Search Trees (BSTs) and the introduction to self-balancing AVL trees.
nodes.title: BST and AVL Trees

nodes.description: Advanced balancing techniques including (2,4) Trees and Red-Black Trees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Red-Black tree properties are a standard component of the cumulative syllabus that every student must know.
nodes.title: Multi-Way and Red-Black Trees
Merge Sort and Selection Sort
nodes.personalizationRationale: Finalizing sorting proficiency with merge sort is a key capstone objective for the course.
nodes.description: Comparative study of merge sort and selection sort, emphasizing divide-and-conquer efficiency.

nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review Capstone
nodes.personalizationRationale: Every student must undergo a final cumulative review to prepare for the required comprehensive final exam.
nodes.description: Final cumulative review of all course material in preparation for the 30% weighted final exam.
